Review Title: Amazon was great, but not a great value anymore
Review Text: I started using Amazon back in the 1990s as a graduate student. I purchased my textbooks there as it was cheaper than the university bookstore and tax free. Fast forward to 2008 when Amazon asked me to try prime for free. I did. And didn't realize they charged me $79 for the membership. I decided to keep it because products were cheaper than at on-ground stores, no taxes and free shipping. Then in 2012 China clamped down on counterfeit producers and stopped them from selling product in China. In 2012 Amazon opened the door to these Chinese sellers and Amazon became flooded with a bunch of junk products. The price of prime kept rising, but I kept it because of Prime video and 2-day delivery. When I became sick I relied on Amazon more. Now Amazon is expensive. They have moved lots of shows to Freevee, which I don't watch because I don't do ad TV. And to add insult to injury this year, 2024, they started adding ads to Prime Video and demanding an extra $3/month to remove the ads, citing all of the other services they added to Prime. I don't use those other services, so it is bloatware to me. Stuff isn't being delivered in 2 days anymore. And there have been times when products were lost in their shipping facilities and not delivered. You call Amazon and they outsource their customer service overseas, these people have no way to contact the drivers. This is rubbish. The seller ALWAYS has contact with shipping! Paying extra for same-day delivery doesn't guarantee it will be delivered same-day. Amazon stopped packing cushioning in boxes so I've received items damaged. I've received spoiled food items. I was horrified to learn the tea I was drinking expired months before. Once they shipped me pet food meant to be sold in Mexico. So, even though you purchase from one seller they ship the product that is closer to your domicile, which might not be the same quality. Prices aren't cheaper than the on-ground store anymore, sometimes it is higher. Taxes are included too. So there is no value to having Amazon anymore. I even submitted my SSN & 1099 to sell t-shirts on Amazon. They stopped adding people to the program that didn't have a huge social media following. But refused to delete my information from their database. Lastly, I purchased a product that was defective, a sports watch. I wanted to exchange it. The watch cost hundreds of dollars. The customer service rep wanted to offer me $25 for it. I demanded a supervisor and the US support team processed the exchange. When Hurricane Beryl was bearing down on Houston TX, I ordered the Midland NOAA radio bundle so I could be notified of tornados and floods should I lose power. My home was hit by a tornado in May 2024, so the threat was real. I paid extra for same day delivery. Amazon split the bundle with one part being delivered in a week and the other same-day, except they never delivered it and promised to deliver it AFTER the hurricane. I called and spoke to three reps. One had a fake barking dog sound and you couldn't hear a word she said. After 30 minutes she just told me to call the number I called to get her. Another promised to expedite it. He didn't. Finally I canceled the delivery with the third person. The product was sitting in Houston, I'm in Houston. I don't know why they refused to deliver it. I had to eventually purchase it from another company. This company that started out well is not the same as it was in the past when it cared about its customers. It doesn't care about its employees nor customers now, it only cares about profit. I will not be renewing my prime membership in October. And I will shop other online and on-ground retailers.

Review Title: How far the Mighty Amazon has Fallen
Review Text: I can't begin to describe how far Amazon has fallen over the years.  I was a customer from the beginning.  I was with Prime shortly after it came out.  I seriously thought it was the best company in the world, until it wasn't.  Then it wasn't even close.  Amazon now has among the worst customer service I encounter anywhere.  It rivals Comcast and Verizon Fios for the worst service you can even conceive of.  There's literally no way to describe the thousand ways Amazon fails at basic stuff.  It's service is a nightmare now.  You're sent off to a foreign country, with people who are supremely unhelpful, with the simplest issues taking hours to resolve.  I'm over it.  I no longer trust Amazon.  It's that simple.  Most recent case in point: I called Synchrony Bank, the issuer of the Amazon store card, to pay my bill.  It said the balance was over $400, so I thought I'd go through to a live person and see what the purchases were, to make sure nothing was unauthorized.  I recognized every purchase, except one.  There was an $11 charge for Amazon digital services.  I knew I hadn't authorized any digital purchases, so told them to put me through to Amazon.  The Indian man I spoke with was completely unhelpful.  Mind you, I mean him or anyone else no disrespect for being foreign.  He spoke with a thick accent likely because English was his second language.  GOOD FOR HIM.  It's something to be proud of.  But it also makes it very difficult to take care of issues that have any degree of complexity at all. He insisted I definitely ordered Amazon Music Unlimited, because I played [unintelligible] on my Alexa device.  What was the name of it?  "It was [unintelligible]"  HUH?  SAY THAT AGAIN SLOWLY?  Literally, his accent was so thick I couldn't tell at all what he was saying.  After repeating it a fourth time, I made out the word "noise."  It hit me that Amazon was charging me $11 a month to play "brown noise" on my bedroom Alexa device.  I've played that as a background sleep noise for YEARS.  Didn't start in December.  I've literally played it for about 3-5 years, every single night.  Suddenly it apparently started charging me for it in December.  I never heard it ask me ANYTHING about a subscription and certainly never agreed to any such thing.  But that didn't convince this Amazon rep, who apparently could read my mind and insisted I absolutely did order it.  I grew increasingly annoyed, especially as he kept going silent for 20, 30, 40 seconds at a time without saying a word, no hold or anything.. just silence.  Finally I told him, "why are you being silent?  I don't know what you're doing."  He then hung up on me.  So much for customer service.  I called angrier now and spoke with a second rep.  She was so very sorry the first rep hung up on me.  If I would just take more time out of my Saturday night to explain everything all over again and verify myself again... which I had no choice but to do.  She took a complaint on the last rep, but said she couldn't help me.  I'd have to be transferred to Amazon music.  Mind you, by this time it's nearly 1 am in the morning on a Sunday morning.  She puts me on hold... and I wait and I wait and wait some more.  About 15 minutes she comes back and says "I'm sorry for the long wait.  I'm still in the queue to speak with Amazon music."  I told her I would wait.  She puts me back on hold... 20 minutes pass... 30 minutes pass... 40 minutes pass.  Finally I had to give up.  She never came back on the line to say anything.  Just the same canned music playing over and over and over and over on a loop.  Called again.  Asked for a supervisor, but my phone died because I'd been held on the line so long.  He didn't call back.  I gave up because I had to give up.  Otherwise, I'd have a stroke from my anger and high blood pressure.  Amazon, you suck. Every single time I have a problem now, this is what I encounter.  Amazon is no longer a great company.  It's a company that will cut every corner, that disrespects its customers and their time, and that cares only about its bottom line.  It will go the way of Sears because it deserves to.

Review Title: They're so bad it's hard to know where to start
Review Text: It's hard to know where to start because there is now so much wrong with this company's services.Having been an Amazon Prime customer for well over a decade I have seen a lot of changes but recently the service has gone downhill to the point that I will not be renewing my subscription when it next expires.Particular issues that I've experiences are:1. Fake products - There are now a large number of cheap/dangerous knockoff products on amazon and it is impossible to tell from the listings which are genuine and which are the fakes.2. Reviews - The review system is broken and now so full of fake and even fraudulent reviews it has lost all meaning. Basic tricks like aggregating reviews for several products or even switching reviews over to a completely different product are common and no attempt seems to be made to stop this practice.3. Prime Delivery - This increased significantly in price and whereas once next day delivery was the norm, the minimum I am now quoted is 3 to 5 days with most items not even despatching for a couple of days after the order - as bad as the free delivery for non-prime members. It is not unusual for items to take two to three weeks to arrive despite paying the Prime premium.I am also seeing a lot of instances where the item goes to "collected by courier" status very quickly preventing order cancellation but no further movement or valid training information appears for several days suggesting that the item has probably not actually been despatched and that status change was just to stop me cancelling when I discover the delay.4. Prime Video - This was always a bit of a rip-off with most items incurring an extra charge on top of prime membership but the latest change forces you to pay an extra subscription on top of the already expensive Prime membership to get the add free viewing I got for free up until now.5. Prime music - this is another service that has been deliberately made almost unusable unless you want to pay yet another addition subscription on top.6. Customer services - All contact is via chat or phone, not email, so hard to make formal complaints or keep a paper trail. Although occasionally helpful, most of the time they merely read information to you that you can already see on the website and promises of action are rarely followed through.I have, at one point or another raised all of these issues with Amazon customer services only to be met with responses that ranged from complete indifference to promises to pass on my concerns which clearly went no further because nothing changed.In short, other than the convenience of having so many items in one place there is little to commend this company any more. Amazon Prime in particular is most definitely no longer worth the money.

Review Text: I have been posting book reviews on Amazon for many years, always buying the books at the site to get the cachet of âVerified purchaseâ. My efforts resulted in more than thirty reviews appearing on Amazon, many rated as either âTop Positive Reviewâ or âTop Critical Reviewâ. But when I submitted a review of âThe Last Politicianâ by Franklin Foer, I got a terse email from Amazon that it could not be posted âbecause it doesnât meet our guidelines for one or more of these reasons: Profanity, Harassment, Hate Speech, Sexual Content, Illegal Activity, Private Informationâ. This had never happened before, and I was quite surprised. I went to the link that showed the âCommunity Guidelinesâ and read all six pages, scratching my head, trying to figure what Iâd done wrong and then I realized the issue was politics. The person checking my review was apparently an extreme liberal so I made some changes that I thought might let my piece âpassâ and I resubmitted it. But I soon realized this was a waste of time because I could make changes piecemeal again and again, but without knowing exactly what in my 850 word review was the âproblemâ, my efforts would be fruitless.How could I get the nameless and faceless Amazon person behind the âwizardâs curtainâ to tell me what to do? I remembered seeing on my âAuthorâs Pageâ a place where I could recommend books. Iâd never used this feature before but now got the idea to cite Franklin Foerâs book as a âRecommendationâ, writing in the comments, âI wrote a review of this book that did not pass the Amazon Moderator and I hope they will tell me what to change.â This was an act of desperation because I truly wanted to get my review posted and I was willing to make rewrites but had to have some guidance, sort of like we got from our high school English teacher who would take a red pencil and underline the problem.Apparently, my ploy with Amazon backfired because I soon got an email saying my post was âoutside of our guidelinesâ and âconsider this to be a first warning.â Amazonâs ire was about the book recommendation Iâd put on my authorâs page (specifically the comments showing Amazon in a bad light) since this was the only âpostâ Iâd ever made other than book reviews.This was going nowhere, and I was not going to play Amazonâs games. I replied to the email, saying, âif you cannot tell me what I am doing wrong I will cancel my book advertising, Amazon Prime, and the Amazon prime credit card and quit making purchases from Amazon.â Six days later I got a reply email saying, âYou have repeatedly posted content that violates our Community Guidelines . . . [and therefore] weâve removed your ability to participate in Community features.â This was untrue because Iâd only made one post, the one where I said, âI hope they [Amazon Moderator] will tell me what to change [in the review that had been rejected].âUnfortunately, all the book reviews Iâd posted on Amazon over the years were deleted. This was quite disappointing because Iâd spent hundreds of dollars on dozens of books, reading them closely over countless hours in order to write honest and informed book reviews and now my work had come to naught. I truly doubt that anyone has put more effort(both in the reading and the writing) into creating a book review than I have. Amazonâs actions have not only hurt me but are a disservice to millions of readers who rely on quality reviews to make wise decisions in their book purchases.As I said earlier, Iâve submitted critical assessments of other books to Amazon and never had a problem and I must conclude the current issue is over politics, simply having a different opinion. While I did say some positives about the author, I also faulted him for being almost sycophantic toward Biden. What he wrote was an uncritical fluff piece and I called it as such. The review, as written, would be passable to any reasonable person and there is nothing out of bounds in it. I read the book thoroughly and wrote an honest, critical review with no malice or evil intent. Review Text: There's plenty to like about Amazon when it works. They sell more or less everything, and lots of it can be with you by tomorrow. But, for a company that is declaring profits bigger than some national budgets, they could shave just a little off that to provide actual customer service, for those occasions when it doesn't simply go right. There simply is no way to get hold of them. If you try to begin a complaint, or ask a question, the site will guide you through a million useless questions, in the assumption that you can only have a problem that they have foreseen, and that you can be guided to an automated procedure. If you really persist, this experience will become circular, as you glimpse buttons that you think will help, but actually take you back to an earlier point in the process. Eventually, you may spot the very well hidden 'contact us' button that appears if you go round three times, and insist each time that your problem isn't listed. Sadly this contact is a chat that is -without wanting to offend those who man cheap call centres - far less intelligent than a bot. Today I had the issue that a number of Kindle books have gone from my library. When you're removing them from a device, one button says, "remove download" whilst another says, "delete," and the latter actually removes the book clean out of your library on the Amazon server. No idea why this would even be a possiblity, let alone so easy to do, but someone in our family managed to wipe a massive chunk of our library whilst emptying a Kindle. It took me about 10 attempts to explain to the guy on the other end that this is even possible - after each attempt he sent me a link to my library, insisting that the books must be there if I bought them. Eventually he pretended the chat had been quiet for too long (5 seconds) and passed it off to someone whose English and knowledge of Amazon was even worse. After reviewing the whole thing again with him, and receiving the same patronisation, he assured me there was nothing that can be done. I told him this isn't correct because I know people who have done it, by virtue of getting a slightly better assistant. Then I provided him with the order number for one of the books that is missing, so he could see that there is still a receipt in my order history, but that the book no longer appears in my library. At this point he told me that Amazon only archive invoices for a year or so, so he wouldn't be able to see a record of the order. I explained that I was looking at the record of the order, by logging into my Amazon account, which resides on their servers, so this was clearly a lie. At that point he simply closed the chat window. Normally I wouldn't go to the trouble of venting somewhere about this, but it's now about the tenth such experience I've had. This one is arguably partly my fault (although there's really no reason to have an option to completely remove books from your library, and certainly not to make it so easily done), but usually it's a complete screw up on their part, and you're still dealing with someone who can just hang up if they don't feel like helping.

Review Title: Great pricing, lack of transparency and accountability
Review Text: While Amazon's prices are normally way better than other companies selling the same thing their delivery system is flawed endlessly. They promise 1-day or 2-day deliveries and 7 out of 10 times they are never delivered in the promised time frame. What they do not tell you is that they have a clause that is not clearly posted anywhere for you to easily say. It says that the delivery time begins when the item is actually shipped. So, if you order an item on a Saturday and it says it will be delivered on Monday by 10 p.m. this estimate will only be accurate if the item was picked up by the carrier on Saturday. Now shipping delays happen and often they do happen as a result of the carrier so that is completely out of Amazon's hands but change the system to more accurately reflect these delays.Quit making promises that you knowingly cannot keep. Additionally, if an item is not able to be delivered because it is damaged in the transit process then include that reason in the email when you cancel the order. This actually just happened to me. In fact, it is the second time in a month that I ordered an item that I never got.Previously I ordered an item that the third-party vendor said was in stock but were unable to fulfill the order because they banked on the parts being in stock when they were going to be shipped. This didn't happen and they simply refunded my money with no explanation as to why.In both cases I had to call the vendor and Amazon to get details on why. Amazon needs to hold themselves and their vendors accountable for the accuracy of their descriptions. From shipping lead times to availability of items.While ordering online is convenient and often times less expensive it is beginning to show the weaknesses that are apparent. At least when you go to a brick-and-mortar store you know whether they have the item and if not, you move on to find it elsewhere.  There is no expectation that you are being told it is in stock when it really isn't. Their inventory is what it is. We are using online services such as Amazon with the expectation that they are going to be upfront with regards to inventory levels and shipping estimates. Not to be told that there are 15 items in stock, or it is a 2-day delivery and then not be able to fulfill these promises more often than not. Quit trying to look spectacular only to look lackluster most of the time. Prices are not everything when you cannot get the items anyways. I gave Amazon 2 stars only because of pricing. However, if the issues continue my 15-year history with them is gone. I will gladly pay more and be part of their solution to the problem by seeing them go the way of K-Mart and Sears.

Review Text: I have a love/hate relationship with Amazon. I order from them all the time, especially the last few years because it is easier than having to go out and search our local stores for particular items, that often times are not in stock or simply not available where I live. I have also often searched for other online stores to purchase items from but rarely do I find one where I can get free shipping and a lower price. So, though it pains me to do so, if I need to place an order for certain items, I shop on Amazon. That being said, the customer service I personally have received has been pretty awesome, the majority of the time. The key is NOT to buy from a third party seller, as that is a huge headache, in my own experience. Also, you cannot write a review that directly complains about Amazon because they will not "approve" it. Which is ridiculous because we all know that Amazon has gone way downhill since the early days. However, that being said, it is possible to get a refund, make a return, and get your money back if you NEVER receive your package. It is a bit of a pain in the a** but it can be done be done. What it takes is patience, persistence, and knowing how to navigate the system. I recently was given a large gift card credit to spend simply because I had such an issue with shipping and it was days past the time my package should have arrived with an item that was an 1/8 of the price of the credit I was given. I used a gift card to purchase it, so I was happy with that. I am the person who manages to get my refunds AND I often get my items for free because I do NOT take NO for an answer. I am polite (for the most part), kind, calm and I do NOT give up. I have experienced many problems with shipping, missing items, items delivered to the wrong apartment, poorly made items, poorly packaged items, products not arriving on time,etc.etc. And each time, customer service has taken care of me. Sometimes it takes more than one phone call and asking for a supervisor, explaining the situation over and over again, but in the end the result is in my favor. I actually fill out the survey the customer service agents email me after the phone call. I am honest and thorough when I fill them out and I praise those exceptional agents who go the extra mile for me, as I appreciate excellent service, as I have been in there shoes in the past. However, if I can find an alternative to shopping at Amazon that also offers free shipping and lower prices, I take it. I would love nothing more than to not have to order another item from them. Obviously, the company treats their employees like crap, the quality of many of their products is merde, they often price gouge, many of their reviews are bogus, the packages are usually not packaged properly or poorly packaged, returns have become a huge pain, many third party sellers rip people off, it can take longer to receive refunds and reviews have to be approved(utter.bullsh**.) Jeff Bezos is making money hand over first, while not paying the amount of taxes or any at all on the billions of dollars he has made and not caring one iota about his employees or his customers. This is what happens when we end up with monopolies and extremely few options available to us. My goal this year is to buy less, continue to search for other online businesses to shop from (especially local ones) and continue to vote, sign petitions and work towards changing the current status quo.

Review Title: Amazon CS Gives False Information and Fails to Find My Package
Review Text: Amazon Pickup Mix-Up 1/3/22I had two packages that were supposed to be shipped out to UPS, one of which was an Amazon return and the other of which would not go through. The package that did not go through contained photos I needed to get developed for a music festival I took pictures for. I owed the organizer images, as I was on the media team for the event. These were to be sent to Georgia. I called UPS to fix the issue with the latter package, and then the following day, someone came to pick up a package. I gave him the film in error, thinking UPS must have solved my issue, only to realize that he came for the Amazon return, not for the film.Calls 1/3/22Following this realization, I proceeded to call UPS, whose representative told me they could do nothing, and bounced me to Amazon, whose representative also told me they could do nothing. I asked her if they could leave something that would let the Amazon shipping center in Virginia (where it was headed) that when they got the package it should be returned to me. She said that Amazon had no such system and I would need to wait until the [package made it to the facility. I asked her if she could put me through to the facility in Virginia so I could tell them myself. She said she had no such ability. I asked if she could transfer me to someone who could contact them. She explained that there was no such person. I thanked her for her time and called UPS again. This time, UPS said they would issue an interception order to stop the package from arriving. I thanked the representative and concluded the call, feeling relieved.Calls 1/4/22The following day, I awoke to find a message from my Amazon app which stated that a refund was applied to my account for my return. Frustrated, I called Amazon again and spoke to someone about the issue. I explained the situation and asked if she could get the package sent back to me. She explained that she was sorry, but the person who spoke to me last gave me false information. There was, in fact, a system of tickets that could be created to notify a shipping facility of a package that should be returned to the sender upon arrival. She told me that since the package arrived at the facility that morning, it has likely been opened, inspected, and the contents thrown away without me being notified. I explained to her that this was a departure from what the other representative told me and that the pictures on the film were for a music festival and were irreplaceable She apologized and said she would file a ticket anyway, just in case, but that I should expect to not get my pictures back. Despite the package being there already (complete with a shipping label and tracking number to aid in its location), she said it would take up to 15 days for the facility to even view the ticket, meaning my package would likely be long gone. She sighed and stated that things "could have been very different" if the first Amazon representative gave me the correct information. I asked why the system takes 15 days when packages are delivered sometimes in less than 2 days. She did not have an answer to this question. Frustrated, I explained that what was originally a mixup due to my lapse of memory has become the imminent loss of irreplaceable photo work and film rolls which were valued at a combined $45. I asked who I should speak to to get compensation for this incident in the event that I never get my film rolls back. She said that there was no such department and that Amazon would not offer compensation because the rolls were no Amazon products. I thanked her for her time and concluded the call. Less than 10 minutes later, I called Amazon support again. I was determined to do everything I could to get my package back. The third representative told me some of the information the second representative gave me was incorrect. She explained that once the package is received by the facility, it is not opened immediately but is rather thrown in a pile with packages to be sorted. According to her, it could take the aforementioned 15 days to find the package and a whole month to return it to me if they succeeded in locating it. She too, however, stated that there was a chance I would never receive it, before doubling back and sending me an email that stated I would get a confirmation email when the package was found.AftermathI am beyond frustrated with Amazon Customer Service. I was given a wealth of false information and every representative had something different to say than the last. No information was consistent and I have barely been given any real help. I am now gearing up for another call to Amazon, in an attempt to speak to a supervisor of some sort. I pray this will bring some sort of positive conclusion to this incident. Those pictures are unbelievably important to myself and my roll as a designated photographer for the festival.

Review Text: Amazon DecrepitudeI had trouble deciding whether to choose one or two stars for my review.In the past you could count on Amazon customer reviews to help you sort out whether a particular item was any good or not. Reviews would tell you about user experiences; how well the product worked, whether there were warranty claim issues, whether the item was suitable for a task, or even if a particular  vendor was untrustworthy or not.However, Amazon started adding Ratings which are not Reviews, simply some useless, lazy person simply giving stars (1-5) without any reason for the rating. Some products have tons of ratings without a single useful note giving a reason for the rating. This is especially infuriating when it comes to reviewing books. You click on what you think is a review and it turns out to be a rating, meaning there is no reason given for the star assignment. This is not very helpful to help you decide if you would be interested in purchasing a book.Later on Amazon removed all of the Comments that customers used to give additional information or commentary on a particular Review. This meant that warning about certain vendors failure to ship products on time, substituting products, shipping used items that were supposed to be new, or explaining why the negative review was a user caused, rather than a product problem.Removing the Comments on Reviews means that a TON OF HELPFUL information is gone resulting in the customer REVIEWS, are no longer as informative and helpful.Of course the worse thing that Amazon had done starting at least 10 years ago is that they lump reviews of different products together, presumably to make it appear that there are more reviews than actually exist. Whenever you purchase an product, you are invited, and encourage to leave a review, which is tied to the purchase of the exact item you purchased so there is no reasonable excuse for claiming that it is hard to connect the review to the exact item purchased. Amazon has all of the data that is needed to do this right.One terrible example of product Review LUMPING are those for Computer Hard Drives (HDs). Amazon lumps the reviews for old generation small capacity 500 Gb HDs, with all hard drives   made by a particular manufacturer with the largest capacity 18TB HDs. Now, the lower capacity HDs were designed and manufactured many years ago, using very different designs and components than those  newest, ultra high capacity HDs. These newest HD's that are very different from the older HDs, and use components that were produced most recently. We know that batches of components of the same design made at different times in factories may have quality control issues, hence Amazon's LUMPING practice defies reason and is DISHONEST.  Amazon will no doubt claim that their filtering menu takes care of this issue, but in fact that is false. You cannot evaluate the percentage of negative reviews (such as adding the two lowest star ratings together) without having these required data easily available. These are not easily found without counting every review. I certainly do not have time to do that, nor should that be required of anyone wanting to understand the review ratings. This would not be a problem if products that are not identical were not LUMPED together.LUMPING is misleading, and seriously dishonest, making it extremely difficult to make choosing a reliable product from Amazon. This practice should certainly stop, and the Review Comments should be put back if possible, and certainly re-instated.I have complained vigorously with customers support and even tried contacting Amazon upper management without success. Do away with LUMPING and get rid of Ratings instead of having Reviews! What will it take to get Amazon to fix these issues ?

Review Text: I ordered a bottle of dandruff shampoo. Around $8.00. and paid with my Mastercard. It came in on time. Instead I got an email from Amazon saying " if you don't pay for the second bottle by (such a date) they would charge me a late fee of $94.00!!!!I didn't want that hanging over my head so I paid for the bottle I never ordered. Around $8.00. No big deal. I received an email from the bank they use to charge credit cards and they confirmed they received my check. I wrote them a check instead of them taking the funds from my credit card.I decided to cancel my credit card but Amazon wouldn't let me. A pop-up came up and said that Amazon requires a credit card so to cancel the card I had to cancel my account.I let it sit as I figured I might buy something later.A couple of weeks after that I received an Amazon credit store card. Only good with Amazon purchases. It was for $600.00! I never asked for this card and if and when I decide to buy something. I didn't know wich card they would bill.When you buy something on credit. You are asked at checkout which card you want them to use.I picked my Mastercard on file. At the same time I deleted the $600.00 card. I did this because Amazon has a reputation of double billing. (Read the reviews). So I immediately locked my Mastercard and had my bank issue a new card with a different number.This at least invalidated my Mastercard and would be denied if someone tried to use it for nefarious reasons.After a few months went by I decided to cancel Amazon completely. Wouldn't you know it had been so long that I had forgotten my password.So I used my email address and pushed the "forgot my password" button. That resulted in my receiving an OTP number.I typed in the OTP number and it took me to a site that had further requirements to make sure it was me. "Okay" I said and I've used 3 different phones over the years.I had to check off my current phone number and nothing happened.My second option was to click on myLG G6 phone. Click? Nothing. I hadn't had the LG 6 for years so that did nothing.My next thing they wanted me to click on my Samsung SE. I haven't had that phone in a long time. I had found my old password.I scrolled down to "cancel your account" I clicked on the bar and it asked me why was I canceling my account. I just typed into the "I no longer want an Amazon account"Another page popped up with the option to change my mind or "confirm cancellation"I hit "confirm cancellation". Done!Another page pops up and asked for my username and password. I just closed out of the page.This morning, while checking my email I seen a "you haven't finished closing your account" message from Amazon.I clicked on it and it started the whole process again. I just deleted the email. It didn't really matter because I had changed the card anyway rendering the Mastercard invalid. I counted six Amazon emails. I blocked them out. So for those who are crying that Amazon closed your account. Count your blessings. They did you a favor. But they still keep your credit card. Don't forget to delete it in the app website if you want nothing more to do with Amazon. Too bad, I had a good relationship with them innitialy. Just wanted to say that you can't ask Amazon to close your account in anger because you feel stiffed by them as they will not close it. Some people here are saying "close my account". That means nothing to them. They've been known to charge over and over and renewal accounts will still be charged even know you tell them to stop. You have to do it on your Amazon website. Just follow the complex account closure instructions.I eventually locked my credit card immediately and ask for a new card with a different number. That will render your card invalid and any charges will be denied. Good Luck as they make you jump through hoops to cancel.UPDATE: 12/25/2021 have not been contacted by Amazon for over a year now.

I check tracking, i talk to my UPS and USPS mail people, i contact possibly 3rd party sellers to find out what's going on before i even "think" of contacting Amazon.Once you have all the possible facts and (again this is KEY so re-read it) you have a "solid" history with them, they will ALWAYS go out of their way to take care of you IF you get a good associate to talk to.Lately, i've been "flushed" by some online chat associates so CALL rather than chat because it's harder for them to make up some excuse about "disconnections" when SOME of these associates (3rd party and out-sourced, you KNOW when you get a good associate vs a out-sourced one) just don't want to handle you.If you come to Amazon "calm" and in possession with as many facts (out of your own investigation) as possible they will work with you and, often, they will drop you some credit to your account for your inconvenience.Now this is not saying that there are no bad associates. Review Title: This morning I found a group packagesâ¦
Review Text: This morning I found a group packages left on the corner of my yard right next to a public sidewalk. Five Amazon Prime packages, for addresses other than mine, had been dumped on my property by, I presume, the Amazon Prime delivery person. I called Amazon Customer Service and spoke to a representative who was argumentative and unhelpful. I explained that these were all Prime packages for people who were paying Amazon a subscription fee in order to ensure quick, safe, responsible delivery. I told her that I live a 15-minute drive away from the Robbinsville, NJ Amazon Warehouse Fulfillment Center at 50 Canton Way and did not understand why this problem could not be resolved today. The Customer Service rep said she would file a report, but did not ask for any of the tracking numbers for the packages. She then told me just to leave the packages outside and someone would be by-- sometime--to pick them up. I waited all day for that to happen.Late this afternoon I called Amazon Customer Service again. This representative was more pleasant and helpful. Apparently, the first Customer Service rep with whom I had spoken did not even file a report when this rep looked to find it. This second rep took tracking numbers with which to file a report and said it would take three days for a pickup to happen for redelivery, which is Amazon's policy, even for Prime subscribers! Again, I said that was unacceptable. For example, Amazon now delivers prescription medications and what if someone is waiting for a prescription to be delivered. I told the rep a three-day redelivery for Prime does not make sense, is bad business, and that I would deliver four of the five packages to the houses whose locations in my neighborhood I know. As for the fifth package, Amazon will actually have to have someone do their job and come to pick it up for redelivery. I also expressed that I do not work for Amazon. With that being said however, the four packages I said I would deliver are now at their correct addresses.Amazon Prime buyer/subscriber beware. I would have left a rating of "zero" if that had been an option. Perhaps Amazon's founder and former CEO, instead of now spending billions of dollars looking for a new planet on which to live (funded in part by Amazon Prime subscribers), should have ensured that Amazon's workforce is valued, not recklessly overworked, that the employees are responsible, and Amazon has logical, work-flow procedures in place in order to deal with problems that are not so difficult to solve.

Review Title: Amazon van drives through our yard, creating ruts.
Review Text: This past week, I was cleaning out my garage, and had one of our cars parked in our circle drive. I heard a vehicle coming down our lane.  I glanced out to see who it was, and saw an Amazon van rounding our circle drive to stop out front of our house, at our front door.   I finished what I was doing at hand, and walked out of the garage, and around front to meet the the driver to get my package. However, before I could get around front, the driver was already back in the van and starting to pull away. Instead of backing out of our circle, because of the car that we had parked there, the Amazon driver simply cuts through our yard to get around the parked car.  I was completely flabbergasted that the driver would do such a thing, especially right in front of a homeowner.  Due to recent rain, our yard was soft, and the van left large ruts in our yard where it drove through.  I tried to pull my cellphone from my pocket quick enough to get a picture of the Amazon van actually in the grass, but by the time I was able to bring my phone up and snap a picture, the van had gotten just beyond our grass and back in the driveway. Nevertheless, you can clearly see the damage, the trail of mud and water in the foreground and the Amazon van in the background, just beyond it.  Had I been a little younger, and faster on my feet, I would have chased the van to the end of the driveway where it stopped for a second, and confronted the driver.   Instead I chose to immediately call Amazon customer service and file a complaint. I sent the pictures, and my eyewitness testimony of the incident to the rep. Nevertheless, the old saying that the customer is always right, does not hold true with Amazon. They basically called me a liar, and said the driver denies driving through our yard, and added that the photos and my eyewitness testimony are not enough evidence, and dropped the claim.  If a representative from Amazon were to come out and look where the van is in the picture, where the damage was done, and note how the driveway is laid out, it's clear that he he or she had to have gone through our yard to either turn around, or otherwise go through our yard to get around the parked car and back on that part of our driveway, but Amazon wanted nothing to do with a little legwork on their part.  We had a birthday party scheduled for the following day, and I did not want guests to see the ruts in our yard, so I immediately started repairing them myself, as I was afraid if someone else saw tracks through our yard, they too would think it was OK - and the damage would become far worse. All I really expected from Amazon, to make me feel vindicated and satisfied, was an apology, and maybe a small credit for a future purchase ($50), for my time having to fix my own yard. But the Amazon representative didn't even ask what they could do to make it right. Instead, they shrugged off a loyal customer as a liar and closed the case. My response to Amazon was that I build homes for a living, making a very good, and well above average income, and the pennies I would get from them for fixing my own yard after their van drove through it would be tiny drops in a very big bucket of water. The point of my complaint was for them to acknowledge what had happened, make sure they communicate with their drivers about the importance of staying out of people's yards, and a very small form of compensation for my trouble. The compensation is of no value to me, but merely viewed by me as a method to set an example for them and their disrespectful drivers. Instead, they chose to side with their lying driver. This decision does little harm to me, as there is literally nothing Amazon sells that I can't buy elsewhere. With that, and additionally in my response to Amazon, I told them that I would never buy anything from Amazon again, and that I was banning Amazon vehicles and employees from our property. If someone else orders something to be delivered to our house through them, or if Amazon is contracted by another company to deliver, and I catch them on my property, I will call the police and file trespassing charges. This includes using our driveway- or yard as any form of turnaround. I will also be setting up static cameras to monitor my driveway and property. All of our friends and family will be made aware of this situation, and advised not to ship anything to our address from Amazon. Amazon would rather lose a loyal customer permanently, than acknowledge that their driver did something wrong, and take responsibility for that action. To me, that speaks volumes of the character of Amazon as a business. I would give Amazon ZERO stars if I could, but my justification is knowing that I can close my account, and take my business -and my money- elsewhere.F.O. Review Title: Greatest e-commerce site. Just a couple of tips though:
Review Text: I've been ordering from Amazon for about 5 years now. I have ordered a variety of products, from dog shampoo to Pokemon products. There were a few instances where I ordered something that I ended up festering an allergic reaction to. Even though the listing said no returns, I was able to speak with Amazon customer service via CHAT (THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT PART, SO READ CAREFULLY). I have had ZERO complaints about Amazon customer service. Why? I NEVER get angry at the rep. Doesn't matter if they are Indian or not. Be courteous and polite when conversing with the rep. Don't be a Karen. Do not ask for the manager cause you won't be getting one. The fate of your complaint pretty much rests in their hands. Act like a beech, you won't be provided any resolution whatsoever. You're talking to a stranger, so make sure you have some manners!!! They are not your child, so stop reprimanding them!When returning multiple products, MAKE SURE THAT YOU DIVIDE THEM OUT ACCORDING TO THEIR ORDERS!!!! Throwing in items from multiple orders into a box is actually wrong, I've learned this from an Amazon rep. Doing so will not only ensure that you will NOT get a timely refund, but it creates more work for the people in the Amazon returns department who then have to manually look through your entire order history and match them up. In a busy work environment nobody wants to have to do that. Another thing that people seem to be missing: when returning an item pack the items CAREFULLY. You can initiate a return for a defective/unwanted product, but if the Amazon workers open up your box and find that it is damaged, they will NO LONGER refund you, they have implemented this policy a few years back. So make sure you pack your items carefully. Don't just toss them in a box without any cushioning/padding and then call it a day. Another thing that I've seen too many Amazon shoppers do is that they FAIL to read reviews before purchasing. That item is 3 stars for a reason! Don't just buy it because it looks like it works/is authentic. Too often I'm seeing people write negative reviews for an already terrible product because they failed to read the reviews. The reviews are there for a reason, and should guide you in your purchase making. It's like buying the first car you see because you like the way it looks, then coming back to the dealership the next day because you discovered that you're too small/big to fit properly in the driver's seat. Be a SMART buyer, not a DUMB one. As a suggestion, Amazon needs to invest in a 'cooling warehouse' for perishable products such as skincare, which lose their efficacy by a large margin when exposed to heat. I order skincare products from their respective retailers now since I keep receiving products that are extremely hot to the touch, even though they were probably sitting in a (hopefully) air-conditioned Amazon van.

Review Text: I purchased a 6 ft Lifetime folding picnic table from Amazon.com with a total billing of $224.69. A Amazon delivery cargo truck pulled up to the end of my 340 ft long driveway in February at about 9 am. It has snowed (3") in the early morning and temperatures hovered below freezing. After calling Amazon and reporting the event, they agreed to accept the package return if there was any damages. There was and it was picked up by UPS a couple days later, shrink wrapped as the cardboard box was mulch by then.  Two months later, I receive notice of a $179.75 refund.  After 15 minutes of trying to find some means of contacting Amazon.... I text conversation to a Customer Service person who refunded the balance citing they had deducted a Re Stocking fee from the original refund.    Long message but.... their drivers need training in material handling and customer service. Amazon is difficult at best to contact if you have an issue and I hope to never see another delivery from an Amazon truck (their local center has been told this directly).  I will admit that once you do get to talk to someone, they do address the issues.... its getting there that sucks.

Review Text: do you subscribe to Amazon PRIME? You might want to read this.For several years there has been a growing issue with Amazon's PRIME subscription. If you were in school however you were appraised with a price of $9.99. while some people left amazon, they have become too big to fail and some of them bit the bullet and just kept the $12.99. as a personal note, it's pretty sad when people will just accept the punishment to stay with a company that has a large and diverse inventory. Many people believe this should change.now recently over last year or so , especially with the covid issue going on people have been noticing that the next day or same-day shipping options are no longer available . this became quite an issue when people were stuck at home and they purchased items that were PRIME-rated , and wanted them immediately and we're more than happy to spend the above and beyond $35 requirement to get them quickly, only to find out, that none of their items would arrive as expected from a PRIME member. Many of the delivery dates now came as short as four or five days later to as far out as a weaker more.many of us understand that third parties are responsible for their shipping and we expect those to take an extensively long time to be delivered, however, when an item is labeled as PRIME, that has been indicated to us that it is in one of the Amazon's local warehouses or at least nearby enough to get them to the customer either the same day or evening or even overnight.another issue with the PRIME membership that has weird its ugly head for quite some time and Netflix seems to have this issue as well as the lack of movies that were allowed to watch with our subscription. almost all the major motion pictures and popular movies and TV shows now have to be rented for $3.99. this is an addition to the subscription fee of the PRIME of $12.99 which means if you want to watch one movie a month you're now paying over $16 for your subscription to Amazon and if you watch more movies for a month just the bill keeps adding up.Amazon has somehow lost touch with its clientele base. So the question remains, what is the purpose of the PRIME subscription if you cannot benefit from it.sadly none of these bad reviews that are actual personal experiences of clients of Amazon will cause Amazon to shut down and or change their policies. as I mentioned before they are just too big to fail and regardless of what your complaint is it will affect them in the least. Amazon has, on numerous times claimed that they cannot show certain movies because of their contract with the movie companies. OK, that is fine, but what does that have to do with the customer, you promised us up to date moves for our PRIME membership - not excuses why they cannot be viewed. Same with shipping. Review Title: I wish that they would let me choose what packaging material I want to use for my order.
Review Text: Amazon.com is a website so huge that its impossible to ignore their impact on society and retail as a whole, they have driven several competitors into bankruptcy including mom and pop stores who cant compete on price, small/medium sized competitors by lowering their prices on products (like baby products) which forces their small/medium sized competitor to lower prices to compete with Amazon and then after they go out of business Amazon will raise their prices when there is no competition around (this has been in news articles). Amazon has also been in the news for things like their poor treatment of fulfillment center employees by timing how many seconds they take to pick an order and pack it, limiting bathroom breaks, and making workers work during Covid-19 even though several of their employees got Covid-19 in their fulfillment centers.  So why do you ask do i keep buying from a company like this? for one simple reason, convenience. Amazon has a huge selection of products, they allow for easy and FREE returns within 30 days where other competitors charge restocking fees for returns and make returns at customer expense for shipping costs. Amazon also has a presence in many countries, ive purchased stuff from Amazon Japan, Amazon UK and had the items shipped to the United States very easily.So why did I rate Amazon.com 3/5? well because while they may be very convenient to buy from they also have very poor packaging and dont let customers specify what kind of packaging they want their items shipped in. Amazon has gotten some heat from environmental groups trying to get them to cut down on plastic and cut down on cardboard boxes in the past and we still see petitions online constantly being opened about their packaging. A simple solution would be to let the customer choose what kind of packaging they want their items shipped in during the checkout process and if theres an extra costs associated with more packaging materials then the customer can decide if they want to pay the extra costs or not. I would totally welcome the ability to choose what packaging material Amazon uses for my orders because I would love to be able to order things like art books, movies, collectibles, and video games from Amazon but whenever I try to order any of these items from Amazon they ship the items in a plastic padded envelope 99% of the time or a cardboard box without any packing paper or void fillers and when I finally receive the item it will be all scuffed up or dented during shipping, have a loose disc (movies and video games), or be damaged in some other way so I would have to go through the trouble of returning the item back to Amazon which isnt good for the environment either since it would costs more fuel and packaging material to be sent back to Amazon. The combination of Amazon's business practices, their poor treatment of fulfillment center employees, and their poor quality packaging which prioritizes getting the package to the customer as fast as possible over the condition that the items arrive in at their destination are the reasons why I gave Amazon a 3/5 score.

In principle, Amazon is not fulfilling the terms of their PAID Prime Service.  I would much rather order a product and get an HONEST, REALISTIC delivery date than continue to get notifications that the product I've ordered is delayed.  In some cases, I would not use Amazon if I knew that my order would not arrive for as much as a week to 10 days after the original delivery date.  Prime is a paid Service, with specific consumer promises.  Amazon needs to fulfill these promises or change them.  In all fairness, prior to COVID-19 the percentages of late packages was probably reversed (20% late/80% on time).  COVID is a challenge for everyone, and Amazon needs to step up to the plate to adjust their business practices to it.Side note:  First tried to review/leave feedback on the Amazon site but I'm ineligible to review Prime Service there. Review Title: Amazon good, lots of room for improvement
Review Text: There are some aspects of Amazon that are fantastic and other parts that are not. This speaks to the character of the leadership (Jeff Bezos) more than anything else. The best part of Amazon is the selection. You can find anything there. And sometimes they even have the best price. The convenience of the site (huge selection) makes me willing to spend a little more, at times. Amazon Prime is nice and gives a lot of great features. Sure the free shipping is nice but not worth the cost of membership. You can still get free shipping, it just takes a little longer. The Prime Video and music help make up the difference. So if you like to watch lots (and I mean lots) of Sci-Fi channel, low budget films then you will love prime video. But remember to keep an eye on your watch list. Amazon has limited time contracts with a lot of content. And thing leave prime all the time.Now for the "Needs Improvement". Amazon delivery and their guaranteed delivery is not so guarantied. The 1 or 2 day delivery begins not when you place the order, but when they actually ship it. To date 30% of deliveries have been late.  Not a day late but closer to a week late. Sometimes even longer. I have had item guarantied by Friday get rescheduled late Thursday or early Friday for as much as 2 weeks later. When this happens I start the return and get it locally (often at a higher price) take of what I was working on and when the item from Amazon finally shows up I take the package and label to UPS or Kohls, whichever is on the label.Now when you call and complain, they may refund your money, if it is a non-returnable, but they do not care that they were late or the consequences of missing a delivery. So a $20 or $30 refund does not really make things right. It never reimburses people who may have been expecting something special (a Childs birthday gift, a Mother's day gift, etc.) or the extra trouble you now go through to make it right for that special person. And to be blunt, it is the lack of empathy or caring on the part of Amazon that is the most depressing and proves that money is the bottom line at Amazon.The delivery drivers vary, some do a great job and show some care when making the delivery and others just toss the package over the fence or onto the porch. Not good when the contents are fragile. They actually ask for feedback on deliveries so maybe this will improve, but I doubt it. When breakage occurs it gets returned.The other down side is they do not allow any negative feedback in any reviews. This is one thing they do not tell you. Just mentioning that Amazon missed a delivery date, or you are less than totally satisfied with your experience, and your review will not be posted. This speaks poorly about the Amazon corp. culture and this is why I doubt Amazon will ever improve. If they were more open and honest with customers we might have more faith in them but that is not the case. You have to wonder what else they are hiding.So my experience is that if it super critical that you get it on time (repairing you only vehicle before work on Monday) get it from the dealer or your local parts source. Do not buy it from Amazon because they will likely miss their delivery.

Review Text: Customer service has gone downhill fast in the past few years from personal experience. Don't get me wrong, I appreciate what Amazon is doing to adjust and accommodate the changes as part of coronavirus pandemic but my issue with Amazon has been going on awhile now. Starting a few years ago I started getting lost packages and receiving other people's packages. Once I even received a package that had my name and address label on one side and another person's name and address on the other of the same package! Amazon has made missing packages relatively easy to deal with by replacing them or refunding them. However, it does make me wonder where the money is coming from, somebody has to pay for the lost packages. Each time I try to contact Amazon asking if they wanted me to return those packages that didn't belong to me the representatives would at first be puzzled and when they realized what I was asking would laugh me off and simply tell me to keep the packages. That was problem number one that got me a bit cautious about Amazon as a company and the Amazon culture. Then it began to become more and more difficult to reach Amazon cuatomer service. The website and app links to reach actual people was convoluted and seemed to change location quite often. There was no easily searchable customer service phone number. Even if you did manage to locate a phone number, the robotic phone tree was impossible to navigate. What made me decide to quit Amazon was when I ordered some textbooks, which mind you, was what got Amazon started in the first place. I ordered the books after school semester had just started and I got the actual textbook list from the professors. Usually campus bookstores are more expensive than Amazon. I hadn't had issues with ordering textbooks from Amazon before (as long as I had the right ISBN code from the professors) until this last time, which was for fall 2019 semester. I ordered the textbooks within the first week of the semester staring. I had Amazon prime and had elected to receive my shipment as soon as possible. A week later, nothing. As I anxiously waited, I got impatient by the end of the second week and called up Amazon. They looked into and said that I had ordered from third party sellers and that there was nothing they could do. They advised that I order only from Amazon and not third party sellers, regardless of what the estimated shipment or delivery showed. This striked me as odd because it sound like Amazon was sabotaging its third sellers even though these third sellers are using Amazon as a platform and paying Amazon (technically speaking the third sellers are Amazon customers in that sense). In any case, I cancelled the long-delayed textbook orders and repurchased them through a seller that I thought was Amazon. It was listed as Book Depository, which when I looked said it was part of Amazon. Turned out that wasn't much better. My books took over a month to arrive. One book was delayed for two months, after which Amazon automatically cancelled the order without recourse. Since those last textbook orders I have vowed to boycott Amazon. It hasn't been entirely successful however. Having been a heavy Amazon customer (my yearly Amazon purchase was probably easily north of 4k) for the last nearly ten years, it has been hard to quit. And I hate it but I have been able to cut my spending on Amazon by about two thirds and aim to cut it down to zero. I think Amazon started off with a simple concept that was utilitarian and expanded to take control of every aspect of consumer life. I suppose it has been successful in making convenience an expectation of many and hence allowing Amazon to tighten its grip. Now that it has a strong grip on so many people, it has cut back or woefully neglected the human aspect of consumption and purchase. It's a shame but I don't think we should continue to award Amazon with our trust.

Review Title: Dismal if things go wrong. Website is part of the problem.
Review Text: Never had a problem with Amazon in the US but I now suspect that was because things never went wrong. Their international shipping and foreign websites are another story because more problems are encountered which their websites and customer service aren't dealing with effectively. I think the sites are evolving as features seem to change. First, the international shopping feature on the US site had issues when I last used them. At least to Mexico. They claim hassle-free shipping and refunds if things don't arrive on one web page but their agreement page states that the buyer is responsible for customs fees and shipping. Confusing and contradictory if not a legal loophole and certainly not 'hassle free". They claim that entering a foreign address for delivery will only allow sale of items that can be mailed to that address. I have had 3 failed deliveries due to orders blocked by Customs. Secondly, their problem resolution via web pages and customer service is difficult, time-consuming and at times ineffective. On one occasion I spent 5 weeks of wrangling for a refund over a $600 order which Amazon Mexico reported had been lost in the (Mexican) mail system. After 5 weeks I gave up on Amazon and went to my credit card company which immediately issued a refund that wasn't contested by Amazon. (Note that refunds of Amazon purchases from third-party vendors are discretionary since they are not coveted by the same rules as direct purchases). Both US and Mexican site had no way of requesting a refund for a lost package. Their AI interface restricts selections and the one page which comes up with a button for lost packages brings up a previous page to repeat an endless and futile cycle. The only page that allows unfiltered contact to customer service is at the very bottom of the first displayed when you select the 'contact customer service" link on the US site. The Mexican site doesn"t allow unfiltered contact. Perhaps Amazon needs to pay heed to the message on their customer service feedback at the end of customer service messages, noting that feedback is helping them construct the 'most customer-centered business on earth.' There are no customer service email addresses or telephone numbers displayed on the Amazon web pages. They can be found for the US and Mexico by doing a web search. Customer service (CS) were always polite and often helpful. However, on one occasion a lost package in Mexico suggests significant chaos and inattentiveness. An ongoing problem isn't followed up by a single person, even when I replied to the specific, numbered email address of the CS representative who emailed me. On each of 5 occasions the reply was from a different individual who, in each case promised that they would personally take care of the problem. I also called a few times and the CS representatives who answered always asked for time to review the case and get back to me, suggesting there wasn't an easily accessible record of the problem or any progress to resolve it. There is a message system embedded in your account information that I wasn't even aware of until a CS representative told me and provided a link. It took a few more days to find a link to it through the Amazon web pages. You can find it by selecting the 'my account' menu. It depends on the app where you will find it on the congested page which is displayed. On some apps it is displayed in the 'My Account' menu. It is an easy way to pick up and reply to messages from vendors but is 'read only' for Customer Service, once again foiling any option of continuity for an ongoing problem. Amazon Mexico fails to correctly identify mail carriers in Mexico, doesn't always update tracking information and later deletes all carrier information. One package was delivered by FedEx, with a FedEx label. My Amazon Mexico order details identified the carrier as Estafeta and provided a tracking number which the Estafeta tracking page said was invalid. My Amazon pages correctly tracked the package and when I used the tracking number on the FedEx tracking, it was accepted and gave identical information to Amazon and more. The expensive lost package was also reported as carried by Estafeta, but with an invalid tracking number. I couldn't check the number on FedEx pages because Amazon had deleted the tracking information from my order details. WHY??? In another case I followed up with a third party vendor on an internationally shipped order through Amazon US because it was a couple of weeks late. Amazon tracking information hadn't changed over the 2 week, indicating that it had 'left the carrier facility in Mexico City'. The vendor reported that a delivery had been attempted and also noted that it was better to track on the carrier's website as Amazon was notoriously poor at updating tracking information.And yes, this account reports Only my own experiences - over about the last six months

However, I hadn't received any knock, doorbell ring, text, or any other notification that the package was delivered, so when I went to step outside of my home around 8PM that evening, my foot ended up right inside of the package which caused me to fall, twisting both legs and causing two sprained ankles, strained knees and hips, and contusions to my knee and ankle. I struggled to get up, but was able to do so with the help of my daughter who came running when she heard the fall. After she got me inside and I was able to get things cleaned up and while waiting for my friend to bring larger bandages so I wouldn't bleed all over my home, and for my daughter's Grandmother to come to my home to take me to the ER since I couldn't put ANY weight on my left foot, I decided to call Amazon customer support to report what had happened. The agent on the other line was apologetic, and advised that she would get in contact with the shipping team, and began asking me questions such as if I felt the driver did it on purpose. I told her I don't think they did it maliciously, but, their negligence in not notifying me that the package was there, and putting it directly up against the step/in front of my door caused injury. I was asked to send in photos so I sent in pictures of the injury, videos of the fall and the delivery driver showing he just dropped the package and walked away taken by my security camera, and photos of my ER visit. Review Title: From "great" to "in the toilet" in three months.
Review Text: The most impressive thing about Amazon.com used to be its unparalleled customer service.  That's the key thing that has kept me a member for 15 years and a Prime member for the last several years.I'm not sure what changed, or why it changed, but since August 2019 that customer service has taken a nose-dive right into the toilet.In 15 years I've only had a handful of Amazon purchases go awry, and in every case I was able to shoot an email to customer service, and within 72 hours Amazon had made good, either by issuing a refund or over-nighting a replacement order at no extra charge.Apparently those days are gone.  Beginning this past summer the email contact option went away.  Also, you can no longer call Amazon directly about an order issue.  The only form of contacts left are on-line "chat", or you can leave them a message and ask THEM to call YOU, at their convenience.Right off the bat this is Amazon telling us that THEIR time is more valuable than OUR time.With email, I could make a report, and check for replies at my convenience.  With "chat" I have to sit by the computer and interact with an Amazon chat person, sometimes for half an hour or more.  In the past 3 months my experience has been that the person you chat with is never able to help you with your issue, without "escalating" your case 2 or 3 times, meaning you get shuffled from one chat-person to the next several times in every chat -- and you get to retell your story 3 or 4 times.Did I mention that before you even get to a chat \person\, you first have to play 20 questions with the chat 'bot?The phone situation is even more ridiculous.   You used to be able to dial an actual customer service rep.  Now you call in a request for them to call you back -- and they return your call, once again, at THEIR convenience, not yours.Even all this might be tolerable had Amazon maintained the same level of service they used to have.  Unfortunately, that also seems to be gone with the wind.Recently I ordered a dozen items in a single order which, for reasons best known to Amazon, was split into two shipments.  One was sent by UPS, and arrived 2 days later without incident.  The other was shipped by USPS and never arrived.  On the third day I contacted Amazon "chat" about the missing shipment and was told that it had "been delivered on Wednesday (the day before).  It hadn't.Amazon chat advised me to wait another day, and then contact them again if the shipment still hadn't arrived.  I waited; it didn't, and I contacted Amazon again.At this point, as recently as last July, customer service would have offered me my choice of a replacement shipment or a refund.This time, I was told to "wait three business days, and contact us again if the shipment doesn't arrive."I waited three more days; the shipment didn't arrive.  I checked with USPS and they told me they had left the shipment "in your garage".  I don't have a garage.  I checked with neighbors up and down the street; none of them had seen the shipment.So, I contacted Amazon chat again.  I was told that I needed to wait three more business days and contact them again.  I did this, and by this point I had waited 10 days for a "2-day shipping" Prime order, which still had not arrived.Since there had been dated birthday items in the shipment, I told Amazon I no longer needed the items, and requested a refund.They told that I -I- needed to initiate an investigation with the USPS, before they could issue a refund.  Excuse me?  -I- was not the shipper of those items; Amazon was the shipper.  Seems like THEY were the one's who should have initiated the investigation.So I said, "fine I'll initiate the investigation, and if you can't issue a refund until that's complete, then please send me a replacement order."I was told they couldn't issue a refund OR a replacement until the results of the investigation were complete.  If you have ever had to have the Post Office investigate a package that you mailed which got lost in the mail, you know such an investigation can take anywhere from several weeks to several months.Everyone of these "chat" sessions lasted a half-hour or longer, and involved at least 4 different Amazon reps.Meanwhile, the bottom line is, I ordered and PAID FOR $200 worth of goods from Amazon which they failed to deliver, and they will not make good on this order until -I- have the Post Office investigate what had to be either Amazon's or the Post Office's screw-up.If someone makes a shipment which doesn't arrive, it is almost always considered the responsibility of the SHIPPER to investigate and make good on the shipment.  Virtually every other on-line seller I use follows this protocol; Amazon used to, as well -- up to this past August.Now it appears their customer service policy is, "we'll take your money, and screw you."Very disappointing.

Review Text: I've first purchased from Amazon in '02, my orders at that point were infrequent and sporadic through the next 10 years, when my kids were very young. However, I became an Amazon Prime member in 2014, and at that point, I started ordering all the time, multiple packages a week, of stuff for myself, my kids, my husband, etc, and started using the same day delivery service all the time. I don't know if there's anywhere that numbers are complied, but I can safely say that I ordered over 100 items through same day delivery, split into dozens of orders. I have been so impressed with Amazon and their ability to keep up with this. I had orders put in by noon, that arrived by 4pm that day, even though it says it will arrive by 9pm. With the thousands of orders they get every day, the reliability and efficiency is unbelievable. No system is perfect, but with the large amount of things I've ordered, I can think of maybe 2 or 3 times that something didn't show up on time, that came maybe a day or two later. This is even with the same day items.A couple years ago, I was staying at my Mom's house, and she lived in a neighborhood that was part of the Prime Now delivery area. I used the Prime Now 1 hour delivery service, and the two hour free delivery, and I made at least 30 of these orders, and never once were they late or incomplete. The selection is limited, as are the delivery areas, but the variety of things they can deliver to your door are really impressive. I've had groceries, household items, sweatpants, t-shirts, work pants and socks for my husband, toiletries, rain boots and various clothes for my kids, cleaning supplies, gifts, etc, all delivered within less than an hour. I now live in the suburbs, out of the Prime Now area, but I still use the same day delivery. The free delivery, even with a short window of two days, isn't something you find everywhere.Nothing is perfect, but the reliability of my deliveries, and the accuracy and good condition of the items, has been about 98%, in the many years, and many, MANY orders. I see a lot of complaints about Amazon, and I just wanted to put in my experience, as some of the complaints are from people who have only used Amazon a couple times, and had a later arrival, or a problem with their order, which is unfortunate, but in a huge operation, there are bound to be flaws, but overall, they offer a service which was previously not available. Also, I get frustrated when I see complaints directed at Amazon, when the order was through a third party, and the both the product and delivery were through another supplier, but the person ordering it didn't even bother to pay attention to this.Bottom line, I'm appreciative of Amazon, and they have definitely been useful to me, and I've gotten my Prime membership fee back many times over, with as many times as I've used the same day, one day, and two day free delivery.

All of these negatives have led to my checking with EBay now and ordering there when they have the same products, which increasingly they do.

Secondly, in the past month alone I have received four items from Amazon that have been damaged to the point of having to be returned. Thirdly, I pre-ordered an item about 3 weeks ago that didn't show up on the day it was supposed to. For the following three days the tracking status showed that the item would be there that day. Yesterday when I went my orders part of my Amazon account this particular item in red writing stated "approval needed". I had to call Amazon to find out what was going on. The gentleman in broken English proceeded to tell me that I needed to call so they knew whether or not to still send the item to me because it was not received on the day it was supposed to. What they were doing was requiring me to call and approve the purchase that I had already made. If I would have not called within a certain amount of time they would have canceled the item all together and not sent it to me. This was a high -in demand item at the time I ordered it. I have a feeling that they sold more than they had in their inventory and are now screwing people over. Whether I receive this item or not is yet to be determined. But, at the end of the day this was supposed to be a Christmas gift for my two year old that she will now not receive this Christmas. I would also like to add that I base a lot of my purchases from Amazon on the reviews.  But I have noticed that when I look at the reviews they are not even for the item that I am looking at purchasing! For example, I was looking at a phone case for my phone and low and behold 80% of the reviews were for a bath mat or a trash can liner. How does a company like Amazon fail so miserably at this? How can you have 5000 reviews for a product and only a small percentage of those reviews are for the actual product you were looking at? The two-day shipping is also a bit of a joke.
